comparison.builder: Arm A has 9/12 strict passes and Arm B 8/12. A adds required question-record dependencies/skip rules and no-tools handoff; B supplies the held-out repository language assumption label that A omits. Both exceed the resume question budget, and neither demonstrates existing-skill file actions. Actual static evidence additionally rejects A’s candidate and baseline folder/name pairs; this does not change its 9/12 pass count.
comparison.domain: Arm A has 5/5 strict passes and Arm B 4/5. A avoids the unagreed glossary action that B adds. The exploratory missing-owner extraction is equivalent in both; it has no predefined acceptance status.
comparison.routing: Both select correctly in all six metadata-routing review cases. Host discovery remains untested.
comparison.multiturn: Both meet the separate scripted multi-turn criteria; candidate asks three distinct first-turn decisions versus baseline two. There is no demonstrated necessity reduction or reliability advantage from this one trace.
comparison.adoption: No all-pass or general superiority/adoption claim is warranted. Original residual failures and unavailable action evidence remain. Single preserved outputs are smoke evidence, not repeatability evidence.
